title: Inhibition of DRP1-mediated Mitochondrial Fission and NRF2/HO-1/GPX4-mediated Ferroptosis by Mdivi-1 Protects Against Vascular Cognitive Impairment.
authors: Liu, Xiao Ming; Chen, Feng; Cheng, Yi Jun; Wang, Da Peng
one_liner_zh: 该文研究Mdivi-1抑制线粒体分裂和铁死亡对血管性认知障碍的保护作用，核心为细胞凋亡与氧化应激，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟方法，仅分子对接为辅助且非针对TF-DNA体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Vascular cognitive impairment (VCI), a consequence of chronic cerebral ischemia, is characterized by an insidious onset and challenging diagnosis. Ferroptosis is a recently identified form of iron-dependent, lipid peroxidation-mediated cell death, and is closely associated with mitochondrial function. While ferroptosis has been implicated in several neurological diseases, its role in VCI remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigated how modulating ferroptosis (ferrostatin-1), mitochondrial fission (Mdivi-1), and Nrf-2 (ML385) affected HT22 cells subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) via the measurement of ROS and caspase-3 levels. A rat model of VCI, induced by bilateral common carotid artery occlusion, was used to assess the effects of Mdivi-1 and ML385 on cognitive function (Morris water maze), neuronal apoptosis, ferroptosis, and the expression of mitochondrial fission-/fusion-related proteins (immunofluorescence and western blotting). Neural damage in the hippocampus and cortex was evaluated via hematoxylin and eosin staining. Mitochondrial ultrastructure and ROS levels were examined by transmission electron microscopy and dihydroethidium staining, respectively. Molecular docking was used to analyze Mdivi-1/Nrf-2 interaction. In vitro, ferrostatin-1 and Mdivi-1 reduced OGD-induced ROS accumulation and apoptosis, whereas ML385 exacerbated these effects. In vivo, Mdivi-1 improved VCI by reducing cortical injury, hippocampal apoptosis, and mitochondrial ultrastructural damage. This was achieved by inhibiting DRP1-dependent mitochondrial fission, promoting MFN1/2 expression, and activating Nrf-2/HO-1/GPX4 signaling, thereby suppressing oxidative stress and ferroptosis. However, ML385 reversed these effects. Molecular docking studies supported a direct interaction between Mdivi-1 and Nrf-2. Thus, targeting DRP1-mediated mitochondrial fission and Nrf-2/HO-1/GPX4-mediated ferroptosis offers a promising therapeutic strategy for VCI.
abstract_zh: 血管性认知障碍（VCI）是慢性脑缺血的结果，其特征为起病隐匿且诊断困难。铁死亡（ferroptosis）是一种新近发现的铁依赖性、脂质过氧化介导的细胞死亡形式，与线粒体功能密切相关。尽管铁死亡已被涉及多种神经系统疾病，但其在VCI中的作用仍知之甚少。在本研究中，我们通过测量ROS和caspase-3水平，探讨了调节铁死亡（ferrostatin-1）、线粒体分裂（Mdivi-1）和Nrf-2（ML385）对经受氧糖剥夺（OGD）的HT22细胞的影响。采用双侧颈总动脉闭塞诱导的大鼠VCI模型，评估Mdivi-1和ML385对认知功能（Morris水迷宫）、神经元凋亡、铁死亡以及线粒体分裂/融合相关蛋白表达（免疫荧光和蛋白质印迹）的影响。通过苏木精和伊红染色评估海马和皮层的神经损伤。分别通过透射电子显微镜和二氢乙锭染色检查线粒体超微结构和ROS水平。使用分子对接分析Mdivi-1/Nrf-2相互作用。在体外，ferrostatin-1和Mdivi-1减少了OGD诱导的ROS积累和凋亡，而ML385则加剧了这些效应。在体内，Mdivi-1通过减少皮层损伤、海马凋亡和线粒体超微结构损伤改善了VCI。这是通过抑制DRP1依赖性线粒体分裂、促进MFN1/2表达以及激活Nrf-2/HO-1/GPX4信号通路实现的，从而抑制氧化应激和铁死亡。然而，ML385逆转了这些效应。分子对接研究支持Mdivi-1与Nrf-2之间的直接相互作用。因此，靶向DRP1介导的线粒体分裂和Nrf-2/HO-1/GPX4介导的铁死亡为VCI提供了一种有前景的治疗策略。
